corrections.reason: By VarBench's own definition DOF is the number of spins and is constant within a file. VarBench README.md (vendor/varbench/README.md, snapshot 390a21e): "`DOF`: number of degrees of freedom. For spins and spinless fermions it is the number of particles, and for spinful fermions it is `Nup + Ndown`" and "Note that all rows in a same file always have the same `DOF` and `Einf`, but we replicate them in every row to simplify data analysis." VarBench paper arXiv:2302.04919 (sources/2302.04919.txt, dated Sept. 12, 2024), Eq. (1) and text: "where N is the number of degrees of freedom, which is the number of spins for spin models" and "For unconstrained spin-1/2 Hilbert spaces, we define N to be equal to the number of lattice sites Ns." varbench-history: DOF column introduced in 107dd73 (Dian Wu, 2022-08-18, "Add DOF to each data row"), where Heisenberg/triangular_12_PP_144.md received DOF = 144 on every existing row. The DMRG row was inserted by c85080f (Dian Wu, 2022-09-03, "Update DMRG baseline for Heisenberg"), a hand-typed line (column alignment differs from the programmatically aligned siblings) with DOF = 100; the same commit replaced the square_10_PP_100.md DMRG row (bond dimension 80 -> 1024, DOF 100, correct there). The cell then passed unchanged through abd23ae (Add Einf, programmatic rewrite), 37648ad (rename to Heisenberg/triangular_144_P.md), 0ef1497, f88f9ba (code link), cd362c4, d186176, fdb4bfb, 5047bfd and 390a21e (snapshot). Never edited, never restored. Across all six VarBench folders the two flagged rows are the only rows whose DOF differs from their file siblings (survey of every DMRG row: DOF = site count for every spin-model DMRG row, e.g. J1J2/square_196_P_0.5 DMRG (bond dimension = 512) has DOF = 196). varbench-methods scripts/Heisenberg/triangular_144_P/dmrg.sh: `julia --project heisenberg_2d.jl --peri --L 12 --J2 1 --zero_mag --max_B 512 --seed 123`; programs/dmrg_itensors/heisenberg_2d.jl builds 12 x 12 = 144 sites, periodic in both directions, square bonds plus J2 = 1 on the (i,j)-(i+1,j+1) diagonal (lines 64-70) and J22 = 0 (args.jl: "Set J22 = 0 for triangular lattices") = triangular lattice with 3 x 144 = 432 bonds of equal strength, Pauli form (`J *= 4`), Sz_total = 0 sector, 50 sweeps, max bond dimension 512, cutoff 1e-12. Prints `energy` and `energy_var` only; no parameter count or DOF, no output log in the methods repo (scope config). QMBL DATA.md: "`dof` is the spin count for spin models"; scripts/units.mjs expectedDof returns n_sites for spin models, so validate.mjs expects 144. Not a duplicate: no other row on Heisenberg/triangular_144_P carries this energy (data/Heisenberg/triangular_144_P.json, 5 rows read).

If the ruling is to keep the flag until VarBench fixes it upstream, the rewritten finding is: "VarBench c85080f (Dian Wu, 2022-09-03) inserted this DMRG row by hand with DOF = 100 on a 144-spin file whose other rows carry 144; VarBench's README and paper define DOF as the number of spins. VarBench's own per-method V-score point for this row is understated by the same factor; the instance-level V-score in the VarBench figure is unaffected (lowest-energy row is VMC with Dirac+field+Jastrow, -314.632)."

compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 144*143/2 = 10296 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 144 exchange proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nkx.driver.VMC_SRt (n_parameters >= n_samples = 1024). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.012 vs sqrt(stored variance 154.749 / 2^20) = 0.012: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 59e621a (2022-09-13, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs). || pass 2026-09-27: evaluation from the script's code path. proposals_per_sample = N x (s + d)/s = 144 x (1 + 0)/1 = 144: batch 1024 = n_samples = n_chains (one sample per chain per step), n_discard_per_chain = 0, sweep_size = hilbert.size = N (NetKet default, every proposal a full forward). sr: n_parameters = 10296 >= n_samples = 1024, so nkx.driver.VMC_SRt: dense Jacobian and the samples x samples matrix O_LT @ O_LT.T per step: kind minsr (verify/agent-A.md item 2). complex false: --dtype default float32, param_dtype=args.dtype, no script overrides it. local_energy all: NetKet's get_conn_padded; the NetKet LocalOperator pads to the batch maximum of nonzero elements, so on Heisenberg/J1-J2 'all' overstates the local energy by about 10-30 % (verify/agent-A.md item 4). Caveat: the scripts (2024-07-30, commit bba4595 the same day replaced cg(maxiter=20) by solve and added VMC_SRt) postdate the 2022 energies; the SR path of the original runs is not known (agent-A.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md).

verified.note: scripts/Heisenberg/triangular_144_P/vmc_jastrow.sh: 'python3 vmc.py --ham heis_tri --boundary peri --sign mars --ham_dim 2 --L 12 --zero_mag --net jas --seed 123 --show_progress' -> 12x12 triangular lattice (ColoredJ1J2 back_diag=False: square grid + (i,j)-(i+1,j+1) diagonals), periodic; NetKet Heisenberg J = 1 in Pauli form with Marshall rotation on the square bonds only (sign_rule=[True, False], a unitary: the diagonals join same-sublattice sites); Sz = 0 (total_sz=0, MetropolisExchange); real float32 Jastrow (nk.models.Jastrow); 10^4 SR steps; final estimate over 2^20 samples (vmc.py lines 268-269). sigma/sqrt(Var/2^20) = 0.988: the stored sigma is the error of that final estimate. 36.7519 above the 2D-RNN record -316.41336(5641) (Moss et al.). M2/M6 flags (if any): real float32 parameters make the amplitudes positive, so on this frustrated lattice the ansatz cannot carry the ground-state signs; no constant shift is involved and the energy is a valid bound.
